adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for SpawnProcess, so hung flushers are never killed before restart and two processes flush the same shards concurrently (duplicate segments, leaked processes).
src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346 — The same isinstance check means join() never terminates spawned flusher processes, so they leak past shutdown and rebalances.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), processes are created via `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, so they will be `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. The shutdown logic only terminates when `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` is true. On platforms where the default `multiprocessing.Process` is not the spawn variant (e.g., Linux defaulting to fork), `multiprocessing.Process` may be a different concrete class than `SpawnProcess`, causing this isinstance check to fail. In that case, when the deadline is reached, the code breaks out of the wait loop without terminating the still-alive spawned processes, leaking them past shutdown/rebalances.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — When the join deadline expires, break skips all remaining processes and none of them get terminated, so processes left from the old assignment keep flushing shards that may now belong to another consumer.

src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:60 — A negative --flusher-processes makes num_processes negative, the map ends up empty, and line 66 raises KeyError; 0 silently means one process per shard because of `or`, and the CLI option has no IntRange(min=1) check.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no range validation, and threads it into `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`. In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` means `0` is treated as falsy and becomes the default (effectively one process per shard), matching the finding. If a negative value is passed, `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))` becomes negative, `process_to_shards_map` is built from `range(self.num_processes)` and becomes empty, and the subsequent loop assigns `process_index = i % self.num_processes` and then indexes `self.process_to_shards_map[process_index]`, which will raise `KeyError` because the map is empty. This is a real crashable edge case introduced by the new option.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:237 — Restart counters are per process and never reset, so a consumer can now absorb N*MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS crashes before failing, while one lifetime-flaky process eventually kills the consumer.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the restart counter was changed from a single `self.process_restarts` int to a per-process dict (`self.process_restarts = {process_index: 0 ...}`). In `_ensure_processes_alive`, the threshold check/raise is now applied per process (`if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...; self.process_restarts[process_index] += 1`). This does mean the consumer could tolerate up to roughly `num_processes * MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` total crashes if crashes are spread across processes, which is a behavior change and an operational/reliability concern, but the diff does not establish that this is incorrect (per-process restart budgets can be intentional). Also, counters not being reset after healthy periods matches prior behavior (previous `self.process_restarts` also only ever incremented).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:257 — In thread mode (produce_to_pipe), a hung flusher thread cannot be killed, so each restart adds another live thread flushing the same shards.

adjudication.rationale: In thread mode (`produce_to_pipe is not None`), `_create_process_for_shards` creates a `threading.Thread` and stores it in `self.processes`. When `_ensure_processes_alive` detects the thread is dead/hung, it only attempts `process.kill()` if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` and otherwise proceeds to `_create_process_for_shards(...)` without any mechanism to stop/terminate the prior thread. This means a hung thread cannot be killed and a restart can spawn an additional live thread handling the same `shards` list, causing concurrent flushing/producing for the same shards.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:115 — One shared current_drift and stopped value covers all processes, and the per-shard drift is lost, so a partition that lags forces early or late flushes on shards that did not lag.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `self.stopped` and `self.current_drift` are single `multiprocessing.Value`s shared across all flusher processes (created once in `__init__` and passed to each worker), but there is no evidence in the diff that `current_drift` was ever per-shard or that it is derived from per-partition lag. Before this change there was only one flusher process and `current_drift` was already global (tests still set `fac._flusher.current_drift.value = 9000`). The claim that “per-shard drift is lost” and that one lagging partition forces early/late flushes on other shards is not verifiable from the provided diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:115 — test_flusher_processes_limit checks only the shape of the shard map; it never checks that segments are flushed from every shard or that restarts, health checks, or backpressure work with multiple processes.

adjudication.rationale: In `test_flusher_processes_limit`, the new assertions only verify `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that `process_to_shards_map` covers all 4 shards via a count (`total_shards == 4`). The test does not drive any per-shard flushing/producing behavior or exercise multi-process-specific logic added in the diff (e.g., `_ensure_processes_alive` restart paths, per-process `process_healthy_since`/`process_backpressure_since`, or backpressure behavior when one process lags). Given the substantial new multiprocessing/shard-distribution logic in `SpanFlusher`, this is a concrete gap in coverage rather than a demonstrated functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:83 — The backpressure assertion was weakened to any(), so a regression where only some processes report backpressure still passes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff replaces a single `backpressure_since` value with per-process state: `process_backpressure_since: {process_index: mp_context.Value(...)}`. The test change from `assert flusher.backpressure_since.value` to `assert any(x.value for x in flusher.process_backpressure_since.values())` is consistent with that new design. Nothing in the diff establishes that *all* processes must report backpressure simultaneously; in fact, `submit()` treats backpressure as triggered if **any** process exceeds the threshold (it iterates and raises `MessageRejected()` on the first qualifying process). So calling this a regression is not verifiable from the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346 — The same always-False isinstance check means join() never terminates spawned flusher processes, so they can outlive the consumer after the timeout.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__` the code explicitly creates processes via `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, so the objects in `self.processes` are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. In both `_ensure_processes_alive()` and `join()`, the code gates termination on `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. Since `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the default-context `Process` class (often `ForkProcess` on Unix), this check can be false for `SpawnProcess`, meaning `kill()`/`terminate()` will be skipped. As a result, if a spawned flusher process remains alive past the join timeout (or is unhealthy), it may not be terminated and can outlive the consumer, matching the finding.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new CLI option `--flusher-processes` with `type=int` and no validation (src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py). In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` will keep a negative value (negative ints are truthy). So a negative `--flusher-processes` value can crash during initialization, and the option indeed lacks validation in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:199 — Metric tag key "shards" on wait_produce is inconsistent with "shard" used on produce/segment_size_bytes/flusher_unhealthy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:185 — Tag value is a comma-joined shard list (high/variable cardinality) while flusher_unhealthy tags a single int shard, so the same "shard" tag has different semantics across metrics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:32 — Docstring says "one process per shard" but processes are capped by max_processes and shards are shared round-robin.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher` docstring it now states: "Creates one process per shard for parallel processing." However, the implementation explicitly caps processes via `max_processes` (`self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`) and then assigns shards to processes round-robin (`process_index = i % self.num_processes`), meaning multiple shards can share a single process when `max_processes < shard_count`. This is a documentation/description mismatch, not a functional defect shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/consumers/__init__.py:436 — CLI --flusher-processes default=1 contradicts factory/flusher default of None meaning one-process-per-shard, so the "per shard" default path is unreachable from the CLI.

In the factory/flusher, the default `flusher_processes: int | None = None` flows to `SpanFlusher(max_processes=...)`, where `max_processes` of `None` means `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (i.e., one-process-per-shard) via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` (src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py). With the CLI defaulting to `1` and `type=int`, the `None`/per-shard default path is not reachable via CLI omission, and there’s no obvious way to pass `None` from CLI. This is a real inconsistency/UX/configuration issue exposed by the diff, but not a direct correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — max_processes fallback to len(assigned_shards) then min() again at num_processes is redundant; max_processes attribute stores a value that diverges from the effective count.

If `max_processes` is provided and exceeds the shard count, `self.max_processes` reflecting the configured limit while `self.num_processes` reflects the effective process count is expected and not a verifiable defect from the diff—at most a small clarity/style nit.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:77 — Per-process SpansBuffer copies (self.buffers) duplicate the passed-in buffer, so the constructor buffer is only used for assigned_shards, leaking a confusing ownership model.

Actual work in `submit()` (recording stored segments, memory info) uses `self.buffers`, which are newly created `SpansBuffer(shards)` instances in `_create_process_for_shards`. This establishes an ownership/semantics change where the constructor argument is effectively just a shard list source, which is potentially confusing/architecturally questionable, but the diff alone does not prove it causes incorrect behavior or a leak.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:301 — get_memory_info is called per shard-buffer against the same Redis cluster, so INFO memory runs N times per submit and used/available are summed N-fold (duplicated cluster-wide queries).

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the diff changes memory sampling from a single `self.buffer.get_memory_info()` call to iterating all per-process `SpansBuffer` instances (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`) and then summing `used`/`available`. This makes `get_memory_info()` run once per shard-buffer per submit, which can multiply Redis INFO/memory queries if each `SpansBuffer` talks to the same Redis backend. The claim about “duplicated cluster-wide queries” is plausible from the diff, but the exact Redis behavior of `SpansBuffer.get_memory_info()` isn’t shown here, so it’s best treated as a performance/architecture review issue rather than a proven correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:270 — record_stored_segments now runs once per buffer in submit, turning one pipelined round-trip into N sequential Redis round-trips on the consumer thread.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit, the diff changes a single call `self.buffer.record_stored_segments()` into a loop over all per-process buffers: `for buffer in self.buffers.values(): buffer.record_stored_segments()` (flusher.py around the shown hunk). This does introduce N calls on the consumer thread per submit rather than 1. While the claim that it specifically converts “one pipelined round-trip” into “N sequential Redis round-trips” depends on SpansBuffer.record_stored_segments() internals (not shown in the diff), the increased number of calls and potential added Redis overhead is a concrete, diff-grounded performance concern rather than a correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:93 — Each process (and each restart) builds a new SpansBuffer with its own Redis client/connection pool on top of the factory buffer, multiplying Redis connections per consumer.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show that the flusher now constructs a new `SpansBuffer(shards)` per process/restart in `_create_process_for_shards` (instead of reusing the `buffer` passed to `SpanFlusher.__init__`), and `_create_processes` will create up to `self.num_processes` such buffers. On restarts, `_create_process_for_shards` creates yet another `SpansBuffer` for the same shard set. However, the claim that each `SpansBuffer` necessarily creates its own Redis client/connection pool is not verifiable from this diff (the `SpansBuffer` implementation isn’t shown). So the concrete, diff-grounded issue is the creation of multiple `SpansBuffer` instances per consumer/process, which could have resource/connection implications depending on `SpansBuffer` internals.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — When max_processes is None (factory default) the flusher spawns one spawn-context process per assigned shard, so process count and memory scale unbounded with shard assignment.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.__init__`, `max_processes` defaults to `None` and is normalized via `self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)`, then `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`, which becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)` when `max_processes` is unset. `_create_processes()` then starts one worker per `process_index`, and in the common case `produce_to_pipe is None` this creates `multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process` instances. So process count (and associated per-process memory/overhead) scales linearly with shard assignment by default. This is a real scaling/operational concern introduced by the change, but not a directly provable correctness defect from the diff alone (it may be intended, and a limiting option was added).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:185 — Metric tags use a comma-joined shard list (plus inconsistent "shard"/"shards" keys), creating high and unstable tag cardinality for timers and segment_size_bytes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces `shard_tag = ",".join(map(str, shards))` in `SpanFlusher.main` and uses it in metric tags, e.g. `metrics.timer("spans.buffer.flusher.produce", tags={"shard": shard_tag})` and `metrics.timing("spans.buffer.segment_size_bytes", ..., tags={"shard": shard_tag})`. This can create higher/unstable tag cardinality because the tag value is a comma-joined list of shards (which can vary by assignment and can represent multiple shards per process). Additionally, the diff uses inconsistent tag keys: `produce` uses `{"shard": shard_tag}` while `wait_produce` uses `{"shards": shard_tag}`. This is a concrete observability/metrics-design issue grounded in the diff, not a functional correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:244 — flusher_unhealthy emits one metric per shard with a per-shard tag, adding tag cardinality and N increments per unhealthy event.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a process is unhealthy it loops `for shard in shards:` and calls `metrics.incr("spans.buffer.flusher_unhealthy", tags={"cause": cause, "shard": shard})`. This does emit N increments (one per shard handled by that process) and introduces a per-shard tag value (higher cardinality) compared to the prior single metric without per-shard tagging. This is a performance/observability concern rather than a functional correctness defect, but it is directly introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:278 — Backpressure check calls time.time() inside the per-process loop on every submit instead of once.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.submit(), the backpressure logic iterates `for backpressure_since in self.process_backpressure_since.values():` and computes `int(time.time())` inside the loop each iteration. This is verifiable in the diff and is a minor efficiency issue (time can be captured once before the loop), but it does not change correctness/behavior meaningfully.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — SpawnProcess is not a subclass of multiprocessing.Process, so hung flusher processes are never killed before a replacement is spawned, leaving duplicate flushers on the same shards.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive(), hung processes are killed only if `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)` before spawning a replacement (`self._create_process_for_shards(...)`). But processes are created via `mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, producing `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` instances. `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the default-context Process class (often ForkProcess on Unix), so a SpawnProcess may fail this isinstance check. In the hang case (`cause == "hang"`), the old process would not be killed and a new one would be spawned for the same shards, leaving duplicate flushers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:346 — The same isinstance(multiprocessing.Process) check never matches SpawnProcess, so join() never terminates flusher processes that are still alive.

adjudication.rationale: In this diff, flusher processes are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, so `process` instances are `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` objects. Later, `join()` (and `_ensure_processes_alive()`) gates termination on `if isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process): ...`. On platforms where `multiprocessing.Process` refers to the default-context process class (often not the spawn-context class), this `isinstance` check can be false for `SpawnProcess`, so `process.terminate()`/`process.kill()` won’t run. With `timeout=None`, `join()` then can block indefinitely in `while process.is_alive() ...` if a flusher process is hung.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:341 — When the join deadline expires, the loop breaks and skips terminate() for every remaining process, so hung processes survive shutdown.
matched_golden_ids: Breaking out of the loop when the deadline has elapsed can skip terminating remaining flusher processes, potentially leaving them running after shutdown; consider ensuring termination is attempted even if the deadline is exceeded.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate notes that when the join deadline expires, the loop breaks and terminate() is not called for remaining processes, leaving hung processes running after shutdown—same underlying issue as the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:201 — future.result() has no timeout, so a stuck Kafka produce blocks the flusher forever; only hang detection can recover it, and that kill path is broken.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.main the code waits on Kafka producer futures via `for future in producer_futures: future.result()` with no timeout (diff shows this still present, now wrapped in a metrics timer). This can allow a single stuck/never-resolving produce future to stall that flusher worker until external hang detection/restart intervenes; the diff does not add any bounded wait. However, the claim that the recovery/kill path is "broken" is not clearly verifiable from the diff for the Kafka case (produce futures exist only when `produce_to_pipe is None`, where a real multiprocessing Process is used and `.kill()` is attempted).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:247 — process_restarts is never reset after a healthy period, so sporadic restarts spread over the consumer's lifetime eventually crash the consumer.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, `self.process_restarts[process_index]` is incremented on any unhealthy event and only ever compared against `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` to decide to raise (`if self.process_restarts[process_index] > MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS: raise ...`). There is no reset of this counter when a process remains healthy again (the only “healthy” tracking is `process_healthy_since`, which is not used to clear `process_restarts`). This means restarts accumulate over the lifetime of the consumer and can eventually trigger the RuntimeError even if failures are infrequent. The diff shows this behavior clearly, but whether the counter is intended to be lifetime-based vs “repeatedly in a short window” is a policy/design choice not fully verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:332 — if timeout` treats timeout=0 as no deadline, which turns a non-blocking join into an unbounded wait.

adjudication.rationale: In SpanFlusher.join(), the deadline is computed as `deadline = time.time() + timeout if timeout else None`. This treats `timeout=0` as falsy and sets `deadline=None`, causing the subsequent `while process.is_alive() and (deadline is None or ...)` loop(s) to wait indefinitely instead of returning immediately for a non-blocking join. This behavior is directly visible in the diff and can lead to unbounded waits when callers pass 0.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:259 — The killed process is never joined or reaped before its replacement starts, which leaks zombie processes and their resources on every restart.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive`, when a flusher is unhealthy it calls `process.kill()` (for `multiprocessing.Process`) and then immediately calls `_create_process_for_shards(...)`, which starts a replacement process and overwrites `self.processes[process_index]` with the new handle. The killed process is never `join()`ed (reaped) before its reference is discarded, so its exit status will not be collected and can accumulate zombie processes on repeated restarts. The same pattern exists in `join()`, which waits in a loop and may call `terminate()` but never `join()` on the processes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:207 — producer.close() is not in a finally block, so the Kafka producer is not closed or flushed when the loop raises.

adjudication.rationale: The diff hunk for `src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py` does not show any `producer.close()` call nor the surrounding control-flow (try/finally) around the producer lifecycle. Since the alleged issue (producer not closed/flushed when the loop raises) is not visible or verifiable from the provided diff, the finding cannot be confirmed against this PR diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:218 — _ensure_processes_alive per-process restart (dead process, hang cause, MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS RuntimeError) has no test coverage at all.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new logic in `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` to detect per-process failure/hang, increment `process_restarts`, kill/recreate processes, and raise a `RuntimeError` after `MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS` (flusher.py around the new `_ensure_processes_alive`). The added/updated tests only cover `flusher_processes` limiting/shard distribution (`test_flusher_processes_limit`) and backpressure state (`test_flusher` asserting any `process_backpressure_since`). Nothing in the diff exercises the restart path (dead process), hang path (stale `process_healthy_since`), or the MAX_PROCESS_RESTARTS exception behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:254 — isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) is False for SpawnProcess so kill()/terminate() never run in production, and tests only use threads so this is never exercised.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher._ensure_processes_alive` and `join`, the code gates `kill()`/`terminate()` behind `isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process)`. However, processes are created via `self.mp_context = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")` and `make_process = self.mp_context.Process`, so in production they will be `multiprocessing.context.SpawnProcess` objects. Since `multiprocessing.Process` is the *default context* Process class, `isinstance(SpawnProcess, multiprocessing.Process)` can be false, causing `kill()`/`terminate()` to be skipped even when a process is hung (the `hang` path). That would prevent proper cleanup/restart of unhealthy flusher processes. The tests pass `produce_to_pipe=messages.append`, which uses `threading.Thread` (not `mp_context.Process`), so this path isn’t exercised by the added/updated tests.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_flusher.py:83 — test_backpressure only checks the backpressure_since value and never calls submit() to confirm MessageRejected is raised per process after backpressure-seconds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py:115 — test_flusher_processes_limit only asserts process counts and total shard count, not the per-process shard distribution or that segments from all shards actually get flushed.

adjudication.rationale: The new test `test_flusher_processes_limit` (added in `tests/sentry/spans/consumers/process/test_consumer.py`) only checks `len(flusher.processes) == 2`, `flusher.num_processes == 2`, and that the *total* number of assigned shards across `process_to_shards_map` sums to 4. It does not assert the actual per-process mapping (e.g., that both processes get shards, or that distribution matches the round-robin logic in `SpanFlusher.__init__`), nor does it exercise the flusher to confirm that segments from shards handled by a shared process are flushed/produced. Given the diff adds nontrivial shard-to-process sharing logic in `SpanFlusher` (`process_to_shards_map`, per-process buffers, restart/health tracking), this is a concrete, diff-grounded test coverage gap rather than a verified functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:328 — join() with multiple processes and a timeout (the deadline break that skips remaining processes) is not tested.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new multi-process shutdown logic in SpanFlusher.join(): it iterates over self.processes and may `break` early when `remaining_time <= 0`, which means later processes are neither waited on nor terminated (termination happens inside the loop per-process). The added/updated tests cover `flusher_processes` limiting and backpressure state, but none exercise join() with a non-None timeout/deadline across multiple processes, so this new deadline/break behavior is untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:51 — Edge cases max_processes=None, max_processes > number of shards, and max_processes=0 are not covered by tests.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new `max_processes` behavior in `SpanFlusher.__init__` (`self.max_processes = max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)` and `self.num_processes = min(self.max_processes, len(buffer.assigned_shards))`). The added test only covers a positive limit case (`flusher_processes=2` with 4 shards). There are no explicit tests asserting behavior when `max_processes` is `None` (default), when it exceeds the shard count, or when it is `0` (which is treated as falsy and thus becomes `len(buffer.assigned_shards)`). This is a specific, diff-grounded test coverage gap for newly added branching logic, not a proven functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:127 — _create_process_for_shard is dead code with no callers or tests.

adjudication.rationale: In flusher.py the new helper `def _create_process_for_shard(self, shard: int):` is added, but all restart/creation paths shown in the diff use `_create_processes()` / `_create_process_for_shards(...)` (e.g. `_ensure_processes_alive` calls `_create_process_for_shards(process_index, shards)`). No code in the diff calls `_create_process_for_shard`, and the added/updated tests only assert process counts and backpressure values, not this method. This is dead/unused code (cleanup/maintainability issue), not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/spans/consumers/process/flusher.py:300 — The Redis memory hard backpressure that now aggregates across per-process buffers has no test.

adjudication.rationale: In `SpanFlusher.submit`, the Redis memory hard backpressure check was changed from using a single buffer (`list(self.buffer.get_memory_info())`) to aggregating across all per-process buffers (`for buffer in self.buffers.values(): memory_infos.extend(buffer.get_memory_info())`, then summing `used`/`available`). The added/updated tests cover process-count limiting and per-process backpressure flags (`process_backpressure_since`), but none exercise or assert the aggregated memory-percentage backpressure behavior across multiple buffers. This is a specific, nontrivial logic change without corresponding test coverage.
